# entire-graph — instructions for coding agents (follow directly)

You have a deterministic local code graph: `entire graph` (functions, classes, methods,
types, routes + call/inheritance relations; no network). These instructions are FOR YOU, the
agent reading this file. Use the graph to narrow exploration without trading away correctness.

## The workflow (mandatory for locate/fix/change tasks)

Your FIRST action on any task that requires finding code must be ONE search:

    entire graph search --repo . --profile full --query "<the task or bug in one sentence>"

Then open the top hit's file with your file-read tool (pass a line range around the reported
line), inspect enough surrounding behavior to justify the change, and make the smallest complete
edit. Treat graph output as evidence, not an oracle.

## Hard rules

1. SEARCH FIRST — never grep/find/cat to locate code before you have searched.
2. READ focused source around the result. Widen the check when aliases, generated code, dynamic
   dispatch, or related implementations could matter.
3. Use graph follow-ups only when they answer a real question. For impact or callers, prefer:
       entire graph impact --repo . --symbol X
4. Make the smallest complete edit and check sibling sites or contracts when the task implies them.
5. VERIFY before stopping. Run the most focused relevant test, build, or reproduction available.
   If execution is unavailable, perform a bounded source-level verification and state the limit.
6. Prefer precise queries and line ranges, but never trade resolution for fewer turns.
7. Feature-detect before relying on semantic relations:
       entire graph capabilities --json

## When NOT to use the graph

If the task already names the exact file and it is small, just read it — the graph saves tokens
by eliminating exploration; when there is nothing to explore, skip it.

## Reference

    locate  ->  entire graph search --repo . --profile full --query "..."
    impact  ->  entire graph impact --repo . --symbol X   (one shot: callers, callees, type consumers, data flow, co-change, siblings)
    callers ->  entire graph neighbors --repo . --symbol X --relation CALLS --direction in
    change  ->  entire graph diff --base A --head B --json
    detect  ->  entire graph capabilities --json   (inventory-only languages have no relations)
    stats   ->  entire graph stats --repo .        (human-facing token-savings report; not part of your workflow — do not run it unless asked)

# CLAUDE.md

This file provides guidance to Claude Code (claude.ai/code) when working with code in this repository.

> [!IMPORTANT]
> **AI Collaboration Rule**:
> - **Planning**, **Brainstorming**, **Implementation** and **Bug fixes** are all
>   in scope. Planning is no longer delegated to Gemini (Antigravity).
> - Implementation plans go in `.claude/plans/` (see
>   [rules/planning.md](rules/planning.md)); design decisions that outlive a plan
>   are recorded in `docs/backlog.md`. Open work (stories, tasks, bugs) is tracked
>   in Plane, see the `## Plane` section of the root `CLAUDE.md`.
> - Always refer to [project-context.md](../project-context.md) for global project rules.
>   It sits in this repository, at the root. The absolute path this line used to
>   carry named a GitLab checkout that is no longer where DevDesk lives.

## Project Overview

DevDesk is a terminal-based TUI (Text User Interface) application built with Go and Bubble Tea framework. It provides DevSecOps functionality including:
- System status monitoring (HTTP/HTTPS, ICMP, DNS, SSL checks)
- GitLab integration (authentication, project explorer, multi-select clone)
- Security scanning (Trivy CVE/secret/license/misconfig + Gitleaks secrets)
- Container management with real-time metrics, on Docker or Podman (`app.container_engine`)
- OCI resource management (image scanning, container launching, network inspection)
- Network diagnostics (DNS, route, ICMP, TCP, TLS, HTTP) + real-time port monitoring + this machine's interfaces + local port forwarding (unprivileged, loopback only)
- Multi-context configuration management via YAML
- Local workspaces management with git metadata
- Claude Code session list (`:agent-usage` / `:au`): sessions found on this machine, by project and date, and per session the agent tree (orchestrator and sub-agents: types, models, tokens, share of the total; sortable by Total; also per agent a state (running / idle / done / unknown, idle after 5 min without a transcript line) shown as a status dot in the first column (the `running` dot blinks, DEVDESK-151) and as text, tool calls and duration; and an indicative cost per agent, `Est. cost` (orange from 75 % and red from 90 % of the session's estimated cost, when at least two agents are priced), from prices you write in the context YAML (`agent_usage.prices`, none shipped), with the session's `Billed` cost and `Unattributed` in the header, DEVDESK-47; a `Breakdown` colour bar per agent and, with `tab` inside a session, a Breakdown tab splitting the whole session's tokens by category, model and agent, as a percentage of tokens, DEVDESK-98). An open session updates live: read again every 2 s while active, only what was appended; paused after 5 min with no write and no unfinished sub-agent, or when its transcript is gone (header `Updates › paused`); `ctrl+r` reads it again in full. The sessions list itself is not live.

## Build and Development Commands

Tasks live in `mise.toml` — there is no Makefile. `mise tasks` lists them all.

```bash
# Development (fastest)
mise run dev          # Run directly with go run
go run .

# Build
mise run build        # Build binary to bin/dk
mise run run          # Build and run

# Testing
mise run test         # Run all tests
mise run cover        # Coverage per package
go test -v ./...      # Run all tests with verbose output
go test ./internal/command  # Run tests for specific package
mise run test-race    # Detect race conditions (critical for Bubble Tea Cmds)

# Code Quality
mise run fmt          # Format code
mise run vet          # Run go vet
mise run lint         # MANDATORY before commits - golangci-lint
mise run tidy         # Tidy dependencies
mise run check        # fmt + vet + lint + test in one go

# Installation
mise run install      # Install to $GOPATH/bin
```

`test-race` needs cgo and therefore a C compiler (`gcc`/`clang`) on `PATH`.

## Git, worktrees, pull requests — absolute rules

- Work happens in a worktree under `.worktrees/<branch>`, created from `origin/main`; the main checkout stays clean, on `main`.
- Never push directly to `main`: the Entire mirror rejects it, and so does the `main-protection` ruleset. Everything goes through a PR, merged once `Lint and build` and `Test` are green.
- Always use `gh -R anthnel/devdesk` (`origin` is `entire://`). There is one remote, `origin`; do not add a second one pointing at GitHub.
- A red `Entire Gates` check caused by Approvals alone does not block a merge (Findings, Checks, Up to date must stay green).
- In a sandbox, only commit; the host pushes, opens the PR and merges. Whoever creates a worktree removes it (never `git worktree prune` from the other side). The sandbox creates its own worktree; the host never creates one for it.
- Before creating a worktree or branch, pushing, opening/merging a PR or removing a worktree, load the `git-worktree-pr` skill.

## Releases

Only merging the release-please PR publishes a release; never merge it without the user's explicit agreement. After every merge on main, the orchestrating session loads the `release-flow` skill and checks the triggers.

**not** `@`-imported: an `@` would inline all of it into every session, which is
the thing this split exists to avoid. Read the file that covers what you are
touching, and update it in the same commit as the code.

### Status Monitoring System

**Factory Pattern for Checkers:**
- `internal/status/checker.go` - Main orchestrator
- `internal/status/http_checker.go` - HTTP/HTTPS checks
- `internal/status/icmp_checker.go` - ICMP ping checks
- `internal/status/dns_checker.go` - DNS resolution checks

Each checker implements `CheckerInterface`. The main `Checker.CheckOne()` uses a factory pattern to instantiate the right checker based on `component.Type`.

**Parallel Execution:**
- `CheckAll()` runs all component checks concurrently using goroutines and sync.WaitGroup
- Results are collected and returned as `[]ComponentStatus`

### Component CRUD Operations

Status view supports adding/editing/deleting monitors:
- `internal/ui/status/components/component_form.go` - Form component
- `internal/ui/status/components/confirm_modal.go` - Confirmation dialog
- Changes persist to `~/.devdesk/config.yaml` via `config.Save()`

State flags in Model: `creating`, `editing`, `confirming`, `selectedIdx`

### Credentials Management

No secret DevDesk holds is written to a file DevDesk owns. `internal/credentials`
implements the `Storage` interface three ways and `Select()` picks exactly one —
writing to several at once is what let the old "secure" option store a token in
the credential manager *and* in plaintext:

| Storage | Backend | Notes |
|---------|---------|-------|
| `KeyringStorage` | Windows Credential Manager / macOS Keychain / Secret Service | via `zalando/go-keyring`, no cgo. The default. |
| `GitCredentialStorage` | git's configured credential helper | Only when the helper is not `store`, which writes plaintext. Context-aware. |
| `MemoryStorage` | this process | Last resort, and deliberately worse: the auth view says nothing was saved. |

`Select(context, preference)` returns a `Selection{Storage, Backend, Detail}`.
The order is keyring → git credential → memory; `app.secret_backend` in the
context config pins the head of it (`auto`, `keyring`, `git-credential`). A
pinned backend that is unreachable falls through to memory rather than silently
to the other one.

The router resolves one `Selection` per context and keeps it in
`shared.State.Secrets`. It must be reused for the lifetime of the context — a
second `Select()` call yields a fresh `MemoryStorage` that cannot see what the
first one holds.

`MigrateLegacySecrets` runs at startup and on every context switch: a
`gitlab.token` or `registry.password` left in a context file by an older build
is moved into the store and deleted from the YAML, with the result reported in
the auth view.

## Testing

Test files follow Go conventions (`*_test.go`):
- `internal/command/parser_test.go` - Command parser tests
- `internal/app/app_test.go` - App router tests

Use table-driven tests where appropriate.

**`go test` does not detect races or explore fuzz targets.** `mise run test` runs
only the fuzz seeds, so `internal/agentusage` concurrency tests
(`TestConcurrent*`) need `mise run test-race`. To explore `FuzzIncrementalMatchesFull`
run `go test -fuzz=FuzzIncrementalMatchesFull -fuzztime=60s ./internal/agentusage`.

**HOME is shared across a test process.** `TestMain` in `internal/app` sets
`HOME` once for the whole process, so under `go test -count=N` a test finds
the files its own previous run wrote (context config, forge index cache), and
it fails from `-count=2` while `-count=1` passes (DEVDESK-36). A test that
writes under HOME isolates it with `t.Setenv("HOME", t.TempDir())` and
`USERPROFILE` too; in `internal/app`, call `isolateHome(t)` from
`harness_test.go` (already done by `routerAt`). `internal/ui/setup` is fixed
(DEVDESK-38): its `isolateHome(t)` helper in `model_test.go` is called by the
tests that write under HOME. Other packages whose TestMain does
`os.Setenv("HOME", …)` may have the same default. To find them:
`grep -rn 'os.Setenv("HOME"' --include=*_test.go`, then `go test -count=2` on each package.

**Never get a "free" port by `net.Listen("tcp", "127.0.0.1:0")`, reading the
port, then `Close()`, and letting the code under test bind it later.** Between
the close and the bind, any `bind(0)` can be handed that very port: an
`httptest.NewServer` in the same test, another test, another process on the
runner. The symptom is an intermittent `address already in use`, mostly in CI
(Linux gave the just-closed port back to about 1 `bind(0)` in 7,000; DEVDESK-35,
D85 in `docs/backlog.md`).

- If the code under test takes a port, call `loopback.ReservePort(t)`
  (`internal/testutil/loopback`). On Linux it holds a socket bound with
  `SO_REUSEADDR`, never listening, until `t.Cleanup`: `bind(0)` and `connect()`
  cannot take the port, but `net.Listen` can.
- Otherwise let the server bind `:0` and read the real port, or keep the
  listener open and hand it to the code under test.
- Off Linux, `ReservePort` keeps the old behavior and the window stays open
  (on Windows Go does not set `SO_REUSEADDR`). That is known, not a local bug.
- `internal/testutil/loopback` is imported from `_test.go` files only; nothing
  enforces it yet.

**Test input and colour (DEVDESK-199).** Build keys only through
`internal/ui/testutil` (`Key`, `Keys`, `Type`, `Paste`, `Text`, `IsText`), never a
literal `tea.KeyMsg` or `tea.Key*`. `Key` is strict: an unknown name panics. The
space key is built as a key (`KeySpace` + rune `' '`), never matched through
`String()` (v1 `" "`, v2 `"space"`). The colour profile is forced through
`internal/testutil/colorprofile` (`TrueColor(t)`, `Force()` in `TestMain`), the only
importer of termenv; it is a leaf package because testutil→shortcut→theme would
cycle. `internal/ui/testutil/source_guard_test.go` fails the suite on a hand-built
key, a termenv import or `SetColorProfile` in any `_test.go`. Paste tests
(`internal/app/paste_test.go`, `wrapped_input_test.go`, `component_form_test.go`):
a paste reaches the focused field, newlines become spaces in single-line fields,
and no key action fires (Rule 111).

**Space and key API (DEVDESK-200).** Production code matches the space key as
`keymap.Space`, never `" "`/`"space"`, and reads keys through `String()` only
(no `.Runes`, `.Alt`, `.Paste`, `tea.KeyType` or `tea.Key<Name>`). Two guards in
`internal/ui/keymap` (`space_scan_test.go`, `legacy_key_scan_test.go`) fail the
suite otherwise; limits are listed in `docs/architecture/app-shell.md`.

## Dependencies

Key libraries (see `go.mod`):
- `github.com/charmbracelet/bubbletea` - TUI framework
- `github.com/charmbracelet/bubbles` - Pre-built TUI components (table, textinput, spinner)
- `github.com/charmbracelet/lipgloss` - Styling
- `gitlab.com/gitlab-org/api/client-go` - GitLab API client
- `github.com/prometheus-community/pro-bing` - ICMP ping functionality (maintained fork of go-ping/ping)
- `github.com/google/go-github/v68` - GitHub API client (§3.6)
- `github.com/libp2p/go-netroute` - which interface a destination leaves by, on all three platforms (§3.44)
- `github.com/zalando/go-keyring` - host secret manager (wincred / Keychain / Secret Service), no cgo
- `gopkg.in/yaml.v3` - YAML configuration

## Code Conventions

- Comments: **English only** (Rule 307) — existing French comments are not rewritten wholesale, but any new or edited comment is in English
- Commit messages: **English only** (Rule 307)
- UI text and logs: **English US only** (Rule 129)
- Bubbletea models define their own message types
- Use `theme` package for consistent styling (`internal/ui/theme/`)
- Config changes must call `config.Save()` to persist
- All colors defined in `theme/colors.go`, all styles in `theme/styles.go`
- Message naming: `[ComponentName][Action]Msg` (e.g., `ComponentFormSubmitMsg`)
- Context names: the rule exists twice (`config.ValidateContextName`, `contextcmd.ValidName`); change both or neither (`TestContextNameRulesAgree`). Creation refuses `-`, `new`, `list` (`config.ValidateNewContextName`); loading does not (D91)

## Critical Bubble Tea Rules

**NEVER modify model state inside a Cmd** (Rule 110) - Race condition:
- `Update()` is the ONLY place to modify model state
- `View()` is read-only
- `Cmd` functions do I/O and return messages

**NEVER use `style.Render()` inside `table.Row{}`** (Rule 122) - ANSI sequences corrupt all subsequent rows:
- Use plain text: `theme.IconError + " error"` not `theme.StatusErrorStyle.Render(...)`
- Apply row styling via `table.SetStyles(theme.TableStylesForState("error"))`

**Update() case extraction**: If a case block exceeds 5 lines, extract to `handle[MessageType]()` method returning `(tea.Model, tea.Cmd)`

# Planning Rules

## Implementation Plans

- **Location**: Always write implementation plans to `.claude/plans/` in the current project directory.
- **Format**: Use Markdown format for plans.
- **Naming**: Use descriptive names like `feature-name-plan.md` or `YYYY-MM-DD-feature-name.md`.

## Antigravity IDE Integration

When using the Antigravity IDE extension:
- Save all implementation plans to `.claude/plans/` relative to the project root.
- Create the directory if it doesn't exist before saving plans.
- Plans should be accessible from both Claude Code CLI and Antigravity IDE.

# TUI — Rule index

TUI rules are split across 5 topic files:

| File | Rules | Content |
|---------|--------|---------|
| [`tui-layout.md`](tui-layout.md) | 101, 107, 108, 111, 112, 123, 124, 130, 134, 137, 138 | General layout, keybindings, viewport, tabs, shortcuts header, format descriptions, shortcuts obviousness |
| [`tui-theme.md`](tui-theme.md) | 102, 105, 115, 117, 118, 119, 127, 129 | Colors, lipgloss background, `theme.*` helpers, language |
| [`tui-forms.md`](tui-forms.md) | 103, 104, 113, 114, 120, 121, 131, 132, 133, 135 | Forms, modals, focus, status icons, value cycling, WrappedInput, key assignment |
| [`tui-tables.md`](tui-tables.md) | 106, 116, 122, 125, 136, 139 | Tables, column widths, plain-text cells + color via `Style`, filter bar, body never replaced (spinner or message) |
| [`tui-behavior.md`](tui-behavior.md) | 109, 110, 126, 128 | Bubble Tea (Cmd/Update), scan cache, footer messages (three levels, one component) |

## Critical rules (summary)

**Rule 110** — NEVER modify the model inside a `Cmd` → race condition. Only `Update()` modifies the model.

**Rule 122** — `Cell` returns plain text (it gets measured), color goes through `Style`. A `style.Render(...)` inside `Cell` gets truncated in the middle of its escape sequence and bleeds onto every following row.

**Rule 128** — A footer message goes through `components.FooterMessage`: three levels (neutral info, orange warning, red error), always centered, a single implementation. A table's loading state is shown in the footer with a spinner, never in the body.

**Rule 139** — A `datatable`'s body is always `m.table.View()`, never a spinner or a message: an empty table (loading, nothing to list, a filter with no results) stays a table — a header, no rows. The count goes in `GetHeaderInfo`, the status in the footer.

**Rule 129** — All UI text and all logs in **English US**.

**Rule 133** — `bubbles/textarea` is forbidden. Use `components.WrappedInput` for any multi-line text field.

The per-topic TUI rule files above load when a matching file is read or edited; when reviewing a diff without opening files, read them explicitly.

# entire-graph — instructions for coding agents (follow directly)

You have a deterministic local code graph: `entire graph` (functions, classes, methods,
types, routes + call/inheritance relations; no network). These instructions are FOR YOU, the
agent reading this file. Use the graph to narrow exploration without trading away correctness.

## The workflow (mandatory for locate/fix/change tasks)

Your FIRST action on any task that requires finding code must be ONE search:

    entire graph search --repo . --profile full --query "<the task or bug in one sentence>"

Then open the top hit's file with your file-read tool (pass a line range around the reported
line), inspect enough surrounding behavior to justify the change, and make the smallest complete
edit. Treat graph output as evidence, not an oracle.

## Hard rules

1. SEARCH FIRST — never grep/find/cat to locate code before you have searched.
2. READ focused source around the result. Widen the check when aliases, generated code, dynamic
   dispatch, or related implementations could matter.
3. Use graph follow-ups only when they answer a real question. For impact or callers, prefer:
       entire graph impact --repo . --symbol X
4. Make the smallest complete edit and check sibling sites or contracts when the task implies them.
5. VERIFY before stopping. Run the most focused relevant test, build, or reproduction available.
   If execution is unavailable, perform a bounded source-level verification and state the limit.
6. Prefer precise queries and line ranges, but never trade resolution for fewer turns.
7. Feature-detect before relying on semantic relations:
       entire graph capabilities --json

## When NOT to use the graph

If the task already names the exact file and it is small, just read it — the graph saves tokens
by eliminating exploration; when there is nothing to explore, skip it.

## Reference

    locate  ->  entire graph search --repo . --profile full --query "..."
    impact  ->  entire graph impact --repo . --symbol X   (one shot: callers, callees, type consumers, data flow, co-change, siblings)
    callers ->  entire graph neighbors --repo . --symbol X --relation CALLS --direction in
    change  ->  entire graph diff --base A --head B --json
    detect  ->  entire graph capabilities --json   (inventory-only languages have no relations)
    stats   ->  entire graph stats --repo .        (human-facing token-savings report; not part of your workflow — do not run it unless asked)

# CLAUDE.md

This file provides guidance to Claude Code (claude.ai/code) when working with code in this repository.

> [!IMPORTANT]
> **AI Collaboration Rule**:
> - **Planning**, **Brainstorming**, **Implementation** and **Bug fixes** are all
>   in scope. Planning is no longer delegated to Gemini (Antigravity).
> - Implementation plans go in `.claude/plans/` (see
>   [rules/planning.md](rules/planning.md)); design decisions that outlive a plan
>   are recorded in `docs/backlog.md`. Open work (stories, tasks, bugs) is tracked
>   in Plane, see the `## Plane` section of the root `CLAUDE.md`.
> - Always refer to [project-context.md](../project-context.md) for global project rules.
>   It sits in this repository, at the root. The absolute path this line used to
>   carry named a GitLab checkout that is no longer where DevDesk lives.

## Project Overview

DevDesk is a terminal-based TUI (Text User Interface) application built with Go and Bubble Tea framework. It provides DevSecOps functionality including:
- System status monitoring (HTTP/HTTPS, ICMP, DNS, SSL checks)
- GitLab integration (authentication, project explorer, multi-select clone)
- Security scanning (Trivy CVE/secret/license/misconfig + Gitleaks secrets)
- Container management with real-time metrics, on Docker or Podman (`app.container_engine`)
- OCI resource management (image scanning, container launching, network inspection)
- Network diagnostics (DNS, route, ICMP, TCP, TLS, HTTP) + real-time port monitoring + this machine's interfaces + local port forwarding (unprivileged, loopback only)
- Multi-context configuration management via YAML
- Local workspaces management with git metadata
- Claude Code session list (`:agent-usage` / `:au`): sessions found on this machine, by project and date, and per session the agent tree (orchestrator and sub-agents: types, models, tokens, share of the total; sortable by Total; also per agent a state (running / idle / done / unknown, idle after 5 min without a transcript line) shown as a status dot in the first column (the `running` dot blinks, DEVDESK-151) and as text, tool calls and duration; and an indicative cost per agent, `Est. cost` (orange from 75 % and red from 90 % of the session's estimated cost, when at least two agents are priced), from prices you write in the context YAML (`agent_usage.prices`, none shipped), with the session's `Billed` cost and `Unattributed` in the header, DEVDESK-47; a `Breakdown` colour bar per agent and, with `tab` inside a session, a Breakdown tab splitting the whole session's tokens by category, model and agent, as a percentage of tokens, DEVDESK-98). An open session updates live: read again every 2 s while active, only what was appended; paused after 5 min with no write and no unfinished sub-agent, or when its transcript is gone (header `Updates › paused`); `ctrl+r` reads it again in full. The sessions list itself is not live.

## Build and Development Commands

Tasks live in `mise.toml` — there is no Makefile. `mise tasks` lists them all.

```bash
# Development (fastest)
mise run dev          # Run directly with go run
go run .

# Build
mise run build        # Build binary to bin/dk
mise run run          # Build and run

# Testing
mise run test         # Run all tests
mise run cover        # Coverage per package
go test -v ./...      # Run all tests with verbose output
go test ./internal/command  # Run tests for specific package
mise run test-race    # Detect race conditions (critical for Bubble Tea Cmds)

# Code Quality
mise run fmt          # Format code
mise run vet          # Run go vet
mise run lint         # MANDATORY before commits - golangci-lint
mise run tidy         # Tidy dependencies
mise run check        # fmt + vet + lint + test in one go

# Installation
mise run install      # Install to $GOPATH/bin
```

`test-race` needs cgo and therefore a C compiler (`gcc`/`clang`) on `PATH`.

## Git, worktrees, pull requests — absolute rules

- Work happens in a worktree under `.worktrees/<branch>`, created from `origin/main`; the main checkout stays clean, on `main`.
- Never push directly to `main`: the Entire mirror rejects it, and so does the `main-protection` ruleset. Everything goes through a PR, merged once `Lint and build` and `Test` are green.
- Always use `gh -R anthnel/devdesk` (`origin` is `entire://`). There is one remote, `origin`; do not add a second one pointing at GitHub.
- A red `Entire Gates` check caused by Approvals alone does not block a merge (Findings, Checks, Up to date must stay green).
- In a sandbox, only commit; the host pushes, opens the PR and merges. Whoever creates a worktree removes it (never `git worktree prune` from the other side). The sandbox creates its own worktree; the host never creates one for it.
- Before creating a worktree or branch, pushing, opening/merging a PR or removing a worktree, load the `git-worktree-pr` skill.

## Releases

Only merging the release-please PR publishes a release; never merge it without the user's explicit agreement. After every merge on main, the orchestrating session loads the `release-flow` skill and checks the triggers.

### Status Monitoring System

**Factory Pattern for Checkers:**
- `internal/status/checker.go` - Main orchestrator
- `internal/status/http_checker.go` - HTTP/HTTPS checks
- `internal/status/icmp_checker.go` - ICMP ping checks
- `internal/status/dns_checker.go` - DNS resolution checks

Each checker implements `CheckerInterface`. The main `Checker.CheckOne()` uses a factory pattern to instantiate the right checker based on `component.Type`.

**Parallel Execution:**
- `CheckAll()` runs all component checks concurrently using goroutines and sync.WaitGroup
- Results are collected and returned as `[]ComponentStatus`

### Component CRUD Operations

Status view supports adding/editing/deleting monitors:
- `internal/ui/status/components/component_form.go` - Form component
- `internal/ui/status/components/confirm_modal.go` - Confirmation dialog
- Changes persist to `~/.devdesk/config.yaml` via `config.Save()`

State flags in Model: `creating`, `editing`, `confirming`, `selectedIdx`

### Credentials Management

No secret DevDesk holds is written to a file DevDesk owns. `internal/credentials`
implements the `Storage` interface three ways and `Select()` picks exactly one —
writing to several at once is what let the old "secure" option store a token in
the credential manager *and* in plaintext:

| Storage | Backend | Notes |
|---------|---------|-------|
| `KeyringStorage` | Windows Credential Manager / macOS Keychain / Secret Service | via `zalando/go-keyring`, no cgo. The default. |
| `GitCredentialStorage` | git's configured credential helper | Only when the helper is not `store`, which writes plaintext. Context-aware. |
| `MemoryStorage` | this process | Last resort, and deliberately worse: the auth view says nothing was saved. |

`Select(context, preference)` returns a `Selection{Storage, Backend, Detail}`.
The order is keyring → git credential → memory; `app.secret_backend` in the
context config pins the head of it (`auto`, `keyring`, `git-credential`). A
pinned backend that is unreachable falls through to memory rather than silently
to the other one.

The router resolves one `Selection` per context and keeps it in
`shared.State.Secrets`. It must be reused for the lifetime of the context — a
second `Select()` call yields a fresh `MemoryStorage` that cannot see what the
first one holds.

`MigrateLegacySecrets` runs at startup and on every context switch: a
`gitlab.token` or `registry.password` left in a context file by an older build
is moved into the store and deleted from the YAML, with the result reported in
the auth view.

## Testing

Test files follow Go conventions (`*_test.go`):
- `internal/command/parser_test.go` - Command parser tests
- `internal/app/app_test.go` - App router tests

Use table-driven tests where appropriate.

**`go test` does not detect races or explore fuzz targets.** `mise run test` runs
only the fuzz seeds, so `internal/agentusage` concurrency tests
(`TestConcurrent*`) need `mise run test-race`. To explore `FuzzIncrementalMatchesFull`
run `go test -fuzz=FuzzIncrementalMatchesFull -fuzztime=60s ./internal/agentusage`.

**HOME is shared across a test process.** `TestMain` in `internal/app` sets
`HOME` once for the whole process, so under `go test -count=N` a test finds
the files its own previous run wrote (context config, forge index cache), and
it fails from `-count=2` while `-count=1` passes (DEVDESK-36). A test that
writes under HOME isolates it with `t.Setenv("HOME", t.TempDir())` and
`USERPROFILE` too; in `internal/app`, call `isolateHome(t)` from
`harness_test.go` (already done by `routerAt`). `internal/ui/setup` is fixed
(DEVDESK-38): its `isolateHome(t)` helper in `model_test.go` is called by the
tests that write under HOME. Other packages whose TestMain does
`os.Setenv("HOME", …)` may have the same default. To find them:
`grep -rn 'os.Setenv("HOME"' --include=*_test.go`, then `go test -count=2` on each package.

**Never get a "free" port by `net.Listen("tcp", "127.0.0.1:0")`, reading the
port, then `Close()`, and letting the code under test bind it later.** Between
the close and the bind, any `bind(0)` can be handed that very port: an
`httptest.NewServer` in the same test, another test, another process on the
runner. The symptom is an intermittent `address already in use`, mostly in CI
(Linux gave the just-closed port back to about 1 `bind(0)` in 7,000; DEVDESK-35,
D85 in `docs/backlog.md`).

- If the code under test takes a port, call `loopback.ReservePort(t)`
  (`internal/testutil/loopback`). On Linux it holds a socket bound with
  `SO_REUSEADDR`, never listening, until `t.Cleanup`: `bind(0)` and `connect()`
  cannot take the port, but `net.Listen` can.
- Otherwise let the server bind `:0` and read the real port, or keep the
  listener open and hand it to the code under test.
- Off Linux, `ReservePort` keeps the old behavior and the window stays open
  (on Windows Go does not set `SO_REUSEADDR`). That is known, not a local bug.
- `internal/testutil/loopback` is imported from `_test.go` files only; nothing
  enforces it yet.

**Test input and colour (DEVDESK-199).** Build keys only through
`internal/ui/testutil` (`Key`, `Keys`, `Type`, `Paste`, `Text`, `IsText`), never a
literal `tea.KeyMsg` or `tea.Key*`. `Key` is strict: an unknown name panics. The
space key is built as a key (`KeySpace` + rune `' '`), never matched through
`String()` (v1 `" "`, v2 `"space"`). The colour profile is forced through
`internal/testutil/colorprofile` (`TrueColor(t)`, `Force()` in `TestMain`), the only
importer of termenv; it is a leaf package because testutil→shortcut→theme would
cycle. `internal/ui/testutil/source_guard_test.go` fails the suite on a hand-built
key, a termenv import or `SetColorProfile` in any `_test.go`. Paste tests
(`internal/app/paste_test.go`, `wrapped_input_test.go`, `component_form_test.go`):
a paste reaches the focused field, newlines become spaces in single-line fields,
and no key action fires (Rule 111).

**Space and key API (DEVDESK-200).** Production code matches the space key as
`keymap.Space`, never `" "`/`"space"`, and reads keys through `String()` only
(no `.Runes`, `.Alt`, `.Paste`, `tea.KeyType` or `tea.Key<Name>`). Two guards in
`internal/ui/keymap` (`space_scan_test.go`, `legacy_key_scan_test.go`) fail the
suite otherwise; limits are listed in `docs/architecture/app-shell.md`.

## Dependencies

Key libraries (see `go.mod`):
- `github.com/charmbracelet/bubbletea` - TUI framework
- `github.com/charmbracelet/bubbles` - Pre-built TUI components (table, textinput, spinner)
- `github.com/charmbracelet/lipgloss` - Styling
- `gitlab.com/gitlab-org/api/client-go` - GitLab API client
- `github.com/prometheus-community/pro-bing` - ICMP ping functionality (maintained fork of go-ping/ping)
- `github.com/google/go-github/v68` - GitHub API client (§3.6)
- `github.com/libp2p/go-netroute` - which interface a destination leaves by, on all three platforms (§3.44)
- `github.com/zalando/go-keyring` - host secret manager (wincred / Keychain / Secret Service), no cgo
- `gopkg.in/yaml.v3` - YAML configuration

## Code Conventions

- Comments: **English only** (Rule 307) — existing French comments are not rewritten wholesale, but any new or edited comment is in English
- Commit messages: **English only** (Rule 307)
- UI text and logs: **English US only** (Rule 129)
- Bubbletea models define their own message types
- Use `theme` package for consistent styling (`internal/ui/theme/`)
- Config changes must call `config.Save()` to persist
- All colors defined in `theme/colors.go`, all styles in `theme/styles.go`
- Message naming: `[ComponentName][Action]Msg` (e.g., `ComponentFormSubmitMsg`)
- Context names: the rule exists twice (`config.ValidateContextName`, `contextcmd.ValidName`); change both or neither (`TestContextNameRulesAgree`). Creation refuses `-`, `new`, `list` (`config.ValidateNewContextName`); loading does not (D91)

## Critical Bubble Tea Rules

**NEVER modify model state inside a Cmd** (Rule 110) - Race condition:
- `Update()` is the ONLY place to modify model state
- `View()` is read-only
- `Cmd` functions do I/O and return messages

**NEVER use `style.Render()` inside `table.Row{}`** (Rule 122) - ANSI sequences corrupt all subsequent rows:
- Use plain text: `theme.IconError + " error"` not `theme.StatusErrorStyle.Render(...)`
- Apply row styling via `table.SetStyles(theme.TableStylesForState("error"))`

**Update() case extraction**: If a case block exceeds 5 lines, extract to `handle[MessageType]()` method returning `(tea.Model, tea.Cmd)`

# TUI — Rule index

TUI rules are split across 5 topic files:

| File | Rules | Content |
|---------|--------|---------|
| [`tui-layout.md`](tui-layout.md) | 101, 107, 108, 111, 112, 123, 124, 130, 134, 137, 138 | General layout, keybindings, viewport, tabs, shortcuts header, format descriptions, shortcuts obviousness |
| [`tui-theme.md`](tui-theme.md) | 102, 105, 115, 117, 118, 119, 127, 129 | Colors, lipgloss background, `theme.*` helpers, language |
| [`tui-forms.md`](tui-forms.md) | 103, 104, 113, 114, 120, 121, 131, 132, 133, 135 | Forms, modals, focus, status icons, value cycling, WrappedInput, key assignment |
| [`tui-tables.md`](tui-tables.md) | 106, 116, 122, 125, 136, 139 | Tables, column widths, plain-text cells + color via `Style`, filter bar, body never replaced (spinner or message) |
| [`tui-behavior.md`](tui-behavior.md) | 109, 110, 126, 128 | Bubble Tea (Cmd/Update), scan cache, footer messages (three levels, one component) |

## Critical rules (summary)

**Rule 110** — NEVER modify the model inside a `Cmd` → race condition. Only `Update()` modifies the model.

**Rule 122** — `Cell` returns plain text (it gets measured), color goes through `Style`. A `style.Render(...)` inside `Cell` gets truncated in the middle of its escape sequence and bleeds onto every following row.

**Rule 128** — A footer message goes through `components.FooterMessage`: three levels (neutral info, orange warning, red error), always centered, a single implementation. A table's loading state is shown in the footer with a spinner, never in the body.

**Rule 139** — A `datatable`'s body is always `m.table.View()`, never a spinner or a message: an empty table (loading, nothing to list, a filter with no results) stays a table — a header, no rows. The count goes in `GetHeaderInfo`, the status in the footer.

**Rule 129** — All UI text and all logs in **English US**.

**Rule 133** — `bubbles/textarea` is forbidden. Use `components.WrappedInput` for any multi-line text field.

The per-topic TUI rule files above load when a matching file is read or edited; when reviewing a diff without opening files, read them explicitly.

# entire-graph — instructions for coding agents (follow directly)

You have a deterministic local code graph: `entire graph` (functions, classes, methods,
types, routes + call/inheritance relations; no network). These instructions are FOR YOU, the
agent reading this file. Use the graph to narrow exploration without trading away correctness.

## The workflow (mandatory for locate/fix/change tasks)

Your FIRST action on any task that requires finding code must be ONE search:

    entire graph search --repo . --profile full --query "<the task or bug in one sentence>"

Then open the top hit's file with your file-read tool (pass a line range around the reported
line), inspect enough surrounding behavior to justify the change, and make the smallest complete
edit. Treat graph output as evidence, not an oracle.

## Hard rules

1. SEARCH FIRST — never grep/find/cat to locate code before you have searched.
2. READ focused source around the result. Widen the check when aliases, generated code, dynamic
   dispatch, or related implementations could matter.
3. Use graph follow-ups only when they answer a real question. For impact or callers, prefer:
       entire graph impact --repo . --symbol X
4. Make the smallest complete edit and check sibling sites or contracts when the task implies them.
5. VERIFY before stopping. Run the most focused relevant test, build, or reproduction available.
   If execution is unavailable, perform a bounded source-level verification and state the limit.
6. Prefer precise queries and line ranges, but never trade resolution for fewer turns.
7. Feature-detect before relying on semantic relations:
       entire graph capabilities --json

## When NOT to use the graph

If the task already names the exact file and it is small, just read it — the graph saves tokens
by eliminating exploration; when there is nothing to explore, skip it.

    locate  ->  entire graph search --repo . --profile full --query "..."
    impact  ->  entire graph impact --repo . --symbol X   (one shot: callers, callees, type consumers, data flow, co-change, siblings)

This file provides guidance to Claude Code (claude.ai/code) when working with code in this repository.

> **AI Collaboration Rule**:
> - **Planning**, **Brainstorming**, **Implementation** and **Bug fixes** are all

> - Always refer to [project-context.md](../project-context.md) for global project rules.
>   It sits in this repository, at the root. The absolute path this line used to
>   carry named a GitLab checkout that is no longer where DevDesk lives.

## Project Overview

DevDesk is a terminal-based TUI (Text User Interface) application built with Go and Bubble Tea framework. It provides DevSecOps functionality including:
- System status monitoring (HTTP/HTTPS, ICMP, DNS, SSL checks)
- GitLab integration (authentication, project explorer, multi-select clone)
- Security scanning (Trivy CVE/secret/license/misconfig + Gitleaks secrets)
- Container management with real-time metrics, on Docker or Podman (`app.container_engine`)
- OCI resource management (image scanning, container launching, network inspection)
- Network diagnostics (DNS, route, ICMP, TCP, TLS, HTTP) + real-time port monitoring + this machine's interfaces + local port forwarding (unprivileged, loopback only)
- Multi-context configuration management via YAML
- Local workspaces management with git metadata
- Claude Code session list (`:agent-usage` / `:au`): sessions found on this machine, by project and date, and per session the agent tree (orchestrator and sub-agents: types, models, tokens, share of the total; sortable by Total; also per agent a state (running / idle / done / unknown, idle after 5 min without a transcript line) shown as a status dot in the first column (the `running` dot blinks, DEVDESK-151) and as text, tool calls and duration; and an indicative cost per agent, `Est. cost` (orange from 75 % and red from 90 % of the session's estimated cost, when at least two agents are priced), from prices you write in the context YAML (`agent_usage.prices`, none shipped), with the session's `Billed` cost and `Unattributed` in the header, DEVDESK-47; a `Breakdown` colour bar per agent and, with `tab` inside a session, a Breakdown tab splitting the whole session's tokens by category, model and agent, as a percentage of tokens, DEVDESK-98). An open session updates live: read again every 2 s while active, only what was appended; paused after 5 min with no write and no unfinished sub-agent, or when its transcript is gone (header `Updates › paused`); `ctrl+r` reads it again in full. The sessions list itself is not live.

## Build and Development Commands

Tasks live in `mise.toml` — there is no Makefile. `mise tasks` lists them all.

```bash
# Development (fastest)
mise run dev          # Run directly with go run
go run .

# Build
mise run build        # Build binary to bin/dk
mise run run          # Build and run

# Testing
mise run test         # Run all tests
mise run cover        # Coverage per package
go test -v ./...      # Run all tests with verbose output
go test ./internal/command  # Run tests for specific package
mise run test-race    # Detect race conditions (critical for Bubble Tea Cmds)

# Code Quality
mise run fmt          # Format code
mise run vet          # Run go vet
mise run lint         # MANDATORY before commits - golangci-lint
mise run tidy         # Tidy dependencies
mise run check        # fmt + vet + lint + test in one go

# Installation
mise run install      # Install to $GOPATH/bin
```

`test-race` needs cgo and therefore a C compiler (`gcc`/`clang`) on `PATH`.

## Git, worktrees, pull requests — absolute rules

- Work happens in a worktree under `.worktrees/<branch>`, created from `origin/main`; the main checkout stays clean, on `main`.
- Never push directly to `main`: the Entire mirror rejects it, and so does the `main-protection` ruleset. Everything goes through a PR, merged once `Lint and build` and `Test` are green.

### Status Monitoring System

**Factory Pattern for Checkers:**
- `internal/status/checker.go` - Main orchestrator
- `internal/status/http_checker.go` - HTTP/HTTPS checks
- `internal/status/icmp_checker.go` - ICMP ping checks
- `internal/status/dns_checker.go` - DNS resolution checks

Each checker implements `CheckerInterface`. The main `Checker.CheckOne()` uses a factory pattern to instantiate the right checker based on `component.Type`.

**Parallel Execution:**
- `CheckAll()` runs all component checks concurrently using goroutines and sync.WaitGroup
- Results are collected and returned as `[]ComponentStatus`

### Component CRUD Operations

Status view supports adding/editing/deleting monitors:
- `internal/ui/status/components/component_form.go` - Form component
- `internal/ui/status/components/confirm_modal.go` - Confirmation dialog
- Changes persist to `~/.devdesk/config.yaml` via `config.Save()`

State flags in Model: `creating`, `editing`, `confirming`, `selectedIdx`

### Credentials Management

No secret DevDesk holds is written to a file DevDesk owns. `internal/credentials`
implements the `Storage` interface three ways and `Select()` picks exactly one —
writing to several at once is what let the old "secure" option store a token in
the credential manager *and* in plaintext:

| Storage | Backend | Notes |
|---------|---------|-------|
| `KeyringStorage` | Windows Credential Manager / macOS Keychain / Secret Service | via `zalando/go-keyring`, no cgo. The default. |
| `GitCredentialStorage` | git's configured credential helper | Only when the helper is not `store`, which writes plaintext. Context-aware. |
| `MemoryStorage` | this process | Last resort, and deliberately worse: the auth view says nothing was saved. |

`Select(context, preference)` returns a `Selection{Storage, Backend, Detail}`.
The order is keyring → git credential → memory; `app.secret_backend` in the
context config pins the head of it (`auto`, `keyring`, `git-credential`). A
pinned backend that is unreachable falls through to memory rather than silently
to the other one.

The router resolves one `Selection` per context and keeps it in
`shared.State.Secrets`. It must be reused for the lifetime of the context — a
second `Select()` call yields a fresh `MemoryStorage` that cannot see what the
first one holds.

`MigrateLegacySecrets` runs at startup and on every context switch: a
`gitlab.token` or `registry.password` left in a context file by an older build
is moved into the store and deleted from the YAML, with the result reported in
the auth view.

## Testing

Test files follow Go conventions (`*_test.go`):
- `internal/command/parser_test.go` - Command parser tests
- `internal/app/app_test.go` - App router tests

**`go test` does not detect races or explore fuzz targets.** `mise run test` runs

it fails from `-count=2` while `-count=1` passes (DEVDESK-36). A test that

`grep -rn 'os.Setenv("HOME"' --include=*_test.go`, then `go test -count=2` on each package.

the close and the bind, any `bind(0)` can be handed that very port: an
`httptest.NewServer` in the same test, another test, another process on the
runner. The symptom is an intermittent `address already in use`, mostly in CI
(Linux gave the just-closed port back to about 1 `bind(0)` in 7,000; DEVDESK-35,
D85 in `docs/backlog.md`).

  cannot take the port, but `net.Listen` can.

  listener open and hand it to the code under test.

## Critical rules (summary)

**Rule 110** — NEVER modify the model inside a `Cmd` → race condition. Only `Update()` modifies the model.

**Rule 122** — `Cell` returns plain text (it gets measured), color goes through `Style`. A `style.Render(...)` inside `Cell` gets truncated in the middle of its escape sequence and bleeds onto every following row.

**Rule 128** — A footer message goes through `components.FooterMessage`: three levels (neutral info, orange warning, red error), always centered, a single implementation. A table's loading state is shown in the footer with a spinner, never in the body.

**Rule 139** — A `datatable`'s body is always `m.table.View()`, never a spinner or a message: an empty table (loading, nothing to list, a filter with no results) stays a table — a header, no rows. The count goes in `GetHeaderInfo`, the status in the footer.

**Rule 129** — All UI text and all logs in **English US**.

**Rule 133** — `bubbles/textarea` is forbidden. Use `components.WrappedInput` for any multi-line text field.

systemPrompt:
Tu maintiens la mémoire écrite de l'équipe : ce que le code et l'historique git ne
disent pas (le *pourquoi*, les conventions, les pièges).

## Emplacements (à créer au besoin)

- `CLAUDE.md` — conventions, commandes (build, test, lint), structure, pièges connus.
  C'est le fichier que lisent tous les agents : garde-le court, exact et à jour.
- `docs/decisions/NNNN-titre-court.md` — ADR. Charge la skill `team-core:adr` (gabarit,
  statuts, numérotation). L'`architect` en rédige le fond ; toi, tu numérotes, relies et
  archives.
- `docs/journal.md` — entrées datées (AAAA-MM-JJ), la plus récente en haut.
- `docs/glossaire.md` — vocabulaire métier.

## Règles

- Avant d'écrire, cherche un document existant à mettre à jour plutôt qu'un doublon.
- Une décision remplacée n'est pas supprimée : statut `Remplacée par NNNN`.
- Vérifie chaque commande ajoutée à `CLAUDE.md` (`Bash`) ; n'y mets rien de non vérifié.
- Sois bref et daté. Cite les sources (PR, commit, fichier, interlocuteur par rôle).

## Ne rien supposer

Si une information qui change le résultat manque ou est ambiguë (date ou auteur d'une décision, statut d'un ADR, commande non vérifiable), ne la devine
pas : arrête-toi et rends tes questions en tête de ta sortie, sous **Questions
bloquantes**, chacune avec les options possibles et ta recommandation. L'orchestrateur
les posera à l'utilisateur. Pour un détail sans conséquence, choisis l'option la plus
prudente et signale-la dans ta sortie (`Hypothèse : …`).

82	D39, before them, was the registry browser addressing a group's
83	members one way to browse them and another way to pull them; it is closed by
84	[§3.18](#318-a-registry-member-is-an-address-not-a-url--repo_prefix), which is
85	what it existed for. D40, found the same day and on the same screen, was the
86	thing §3.18 blocked on and had already been closed on its own.
87	
88	D1 through D61 are all fixed or, in D35's case, deliberately
89	downgraded to a stale reading with a way to refresh it. §1.1 records what each was and why the
90	chosen fix was the right one — including the three that were answered by
91	*removing* something rather than making it work: D8's write-only CRUD flags,
92	D21's unreachable clamp and D36's never-filled cache.
93	
94	The five that stayed open longest — D4, D8, D9, D10 and D11 — were parked not
95	because they were hard but because each altered something the user already saw,
96	so they needed a deliberate call rather than a drive-by fix. All five were then
97	decided together and fixed in one pass; see [§1.2](#12-the-five-parked-defects).
98	
99	### 1.1 Fixed
100	
101	**D117 — DEVDESK-201: what is not covered by a test, and what only a person can check. Open.** **Plane:** DEVDESK-201, dated 2026-11-10
102	
103	Not covered by a test, to decide before the story closes: (a) the guard that a key is read through `String()` only (DEVDESK-200) does not cover `.Code`, `.Text` and `.Mod`; either a guard is added or the gap is accepted; (b) 15 `lipgloss.Place` call sites have no dedicated test (the Rule 115 test covers the confirm modal only); (c) `tea.PasteStartMsg` and `tea.PasteEndMsg` are ignored without a test.
104	
105	Manual checks, run by the user and not by the agents (no TTY in the sandbox), on Windows Terminal (`dk.exe`) and WSL in Windows Terminal: the four `tea.ExecProcess` calls (container shell `T`, OCI launch `-it`, viewer pager `V`, workspace terminal `T`: alt screen restored, colours intact, no stray output); `dk setup` (alt screen, fields, space on its confirm, paste); space in every checkbox form; paste in the palette, a filter bar and a form, multi-line paste in a single-line field; one uppercase action (`S` in `ws`) and `ctrl+r`; colours under WSL with and without `NO_COLOR=1`; a VS16 emoji and a Nerd Font icon column with no shift (mode 2027); the textinput cursor background (Rule 115).
106	
107	**D116 — DEVDESK-201: the prudent defaults taken without asking (H2, H3, H4, H6). Decided, to confirm.** **Plane:** DEVDESK-201, dated 2026-11-10
108	
109	- **H2.** The `internal/testutil/colorprofile` helper is a no-op from A2 (`lipgloss.SetColorProfile` does not exist in v2), so the theme, overlay, shortcut, datatable and components tests compile. It is removed in F (`e65ab2f`), with `termenv`. The plan kept it as a no-op for its 50 callers; the branch deletes it.
110	- **H3.** `LoadTheme` refuses the whole theme when a non-empty value is not `#rgb` or `#rrggbb`, and the error names the key and the value. An empty optional key keeps the fallback. Callers are unchanged: `main.go` logs and keeps the default theme, `App.applyThemeNow` logs and keeps the current one. No footer message: a follow-up if wanted.
111	- **H4.** `main.go` forces `tea.WithColorProfile(colorprofile.TrueColor)` when `WT_SESSION` is set and `NO_COLOR` is not. A forced profile bypasses the `NO_COLOR` check of `colorprofile.Detect`, so the condition is explicit. The `COLORTERM` workaround is deleted.
112	- **H6.** `App.setView(name, m tea.Model)` is the only place that asserts `Screen`. A view that does not implement `Render` panics with the view's name; Bubble Tea recovers and restores the terminal.
113	
114	**D115 — DEVDESK-201: three claims of the plan that the branch does not support as written.** **Plane:** DEVDESK-201, dated 2026-11-10
115	
116	1. *The red proof for the `(4)` criterion.* The plan wanted the test that pins the width of a flag or ZWJ sequence to be red on the v2 code before the fix. It was in fact red on `go-runewidth` v0.0.16, the pre-migration version: `x/ansi` v0.11.9 already brings `go-runewidth` v0.0.30 with the v2 stack, so the red state was never shown on v2. Re-check on the migrated code before merge.
117	2. *Width divergence between libraries.* `datatable` measures with `go-runewidth` and the terminal-facing `x/ansi` measures differently for VS16 emoji (`a❤️x`: 3 against 4; `✔️`: 1 against 2). The divergence is pinned by `REDACTED`, so a library fix shows up as a test change.
118	3. *"Identical rendering" of the `ntcharts` sparkline.* Identical glyphs, not identical bytes: the background SGR goes from `48` to `49` and the reset is `\x1b[m`. The plan's "rendu identique" means the cells, not the escape sequences.
119	
120	Also lost: the background of the textinput virtual cursor (Rule 115). bubbles v2 `CursorStyle` has no background; the gap is accepted until the manual check of D117.
121	
122	**D114 — DEVDESK-201: the redraw cost of Bubble Tea v2 against v1 (`TestMeasureRedrawCost`). Measured; the threshold is +25 %; the verdict is within it.** **Plane:** DEVDESK-201 (G2), analysis DEVDESK-201 (perf)
123	
124	Threshold chosen by the user from the three options of the plan (report only; +25 % on bytes/s of `blink-20` or `spinner-20` and no more redraws than the tick cadence). The v2 renderer also writes terminal queries and synchronized-output brackets that v1 does not, so "no worse than v1" would fail on bytes that cost nothing on screen.
125	
126	Bytes/s, medians of 3 runs, interleaved on the same machine (the D110 host). v1 TrueColor is forced (D110 correction); v1 Ascii is the unforced base. Redraws: 2/s for blink, 10/s for spinner, identical in all three.
127	
128	| Case | v1 Ascii B/s | v1 TrueColor B/s | v2 B/s | v2 vs v1 Ascii | v2 vs v1 TrueColor |
129	|---|---|---|---|---|---|
130	| blink-0 | 0 | 0 | 0 | = | = |
131	| blink-1 | 376 | not measured | 84 | −78 % | not measured |
132	| blink-20 | 5809 | 11890 | 1726 | −70 % | −85 % |
133	| spinner-1 | 1880 | not measured | 420 | −78 % | not measured |
134	| spinner-20 | 29046 | 59450 | 8629 | −70 % | −85 % |
135	
136	Bytes per redraw (20-row cases): 2905 Ascii, 5945 TrueColor, 863 v2. v2 repaints changed cells only; v1 rewrote lines.
137	
138	- **Verdict:** within the threshold against either base. Bytes are −70 % or better (Ascii), −85 % (TrueColor), and redraws equal the tick cadence. Nothing rises.
139	- **`View()` cost (D114 perf analysis, DEVDESK-201).** Isolated benchmark, `GOMAXPROCS=1`, 7 interleaved runs: v1 Ascii 288 µs, v1 TrueColor 683 µs, v2 868 µs. Real surcharge against v1 TrueColor: **+27 %**. The "×2.5–3" of the first measure is mostly an artefact: 12 to 60 cold calls, no warm-up. In-program: about 1.5 ms (v1 TrueColor) against about 2.0 ms cold (v2).
140	- **Cause.** `x/ansi` `stringWidth` (since v0.11.7) walks every character through grapheme segmentation, ASCII included: 240 ns to 1310 ns on a 116-column ASCII line; its share of `View()` goes from 30 % to 67 %. The v1 colour conversion (36 % of v1, via go-colorful and `Sscanf`) disappears. The theme code converts nothing per frame. The cost sits in a library: bubbletea v2.1.1 requires `x/ansi` v0.11.9, so it is not avoidable short of an upstream change.
141	- **Impact.** About 0.87 ms warm (about 2 ms cold) per 120×40 frame: 5–13 % of the 16 ms budget, about 2 % of one core at 10 Hz, +0.5 % CPU against v1 TrueColor. **Non-blocking.**
142	- **Not applied (options).** Upstream ASCII shortcut in `charmbracelet/x` `ansi/width.go` (estimated −45 to −55 % on `View`), to report upstream only if the user decides so. `view.go:117-121` redundant `Style.Width` (−6 %, but it changes the padding background: Rule 115, visual check). `lipgloss.Place` in `view.go:34-35` (at most 7 %). Compare the `redraw_measure_test.go` harness under v1 TrueColor for a fair base.
143	- **Harness defect fixed.** Without a TTY, v2 sends its own `WindowSizeMsg` built from a 0×0 size, which shrinks the router to a 489-byte view. The fix is `tea.WithWindowSize(...)` and `tea.WithColorProfile(colorprofile.TrueColor)` in `measureRedraws` (`e44dcb0`).
144	- **Limits.** In-process, no TTY: this counts what the renderer writes, not what a terminal shows. The v2 mode queries and synchronized output are not exercised; the real-SSH check stays with A-06. The `View()` study uses a dummy 120×40 view on one machine; real views are not profiled.
145	
146	**D113 — DEVDESK-201: Rule 135 corrected in the PR. Enter does nothing on a checkbox; Space no longer answers Yes or No on a confirmation. Decided (prudent choice on a destructive modal, to confirm).** **Plane:** DEVDESK-201 (`ad0900d`), dated 2026-11-10
147	
148	Rule 135 gives `Space` alone the tick on a checkbox and `Enter` alone the validation of action buttons. The v2 port exposed two places where the rule was not applied:
149	- Enter toggled a checkbox. It is now ignored on a checkbox cell.
150	- Space answered the focused Yes or No button of `OptionConfirmModal`, `ConfirmModal`, `ChoiceModal` and the setup wizard's `confirm`. It no longer does.
151	
152	Choice on a destructive modal: Enter on a focused cell is ignored rather than advancing to the next step, so a stray Enter cannot confirm a delete. The alternative (Enter advances, as on any other button) is open to the user; it changes one line per modal.
153	
154	Rule 135 text to be corrected by the tech-writer (G1): the Space line becomes `keymap.Space` is `"space"`, the key is matched through the constant.
155	
156	**D112 — DEVDESK-201: the Charm v2 migration lands as one pull request, in categories; the commits are review units. Decided.** **Plane:** DEVDESK-201, dated 2026-11-10
157	
158	One PR, squash-merged, with the commits listed in its body. The commits split the migration by category, not by file, and they are not bisect points: `internal/app` imports every view, so no commit between the imports change and the theme change builds the whole module. Real order on `feat/DEVDESK-201-charm-v2`, after `origin/main` `f8c3063`:
159	
160	`7091e78` imports and `go.mod` (A1) → `a74a262` theme `color.Color` and hex validation (A2) → `0692c35` keys, `KeyPressMsg`, `keymap.Space = "space"` (B) → `ba1d938` Bubbles and Lip Gloss APIs (D1) → `495409b` ntcharts v2 and module tidy (E) → `89f32a3` `Render` and `View() tea.View`, router owns `AltScreen` (C) → `dab9d28` fix: nil `confirmModal` guard removed from the setup wizard render → `ad0900d` Rule 135 (B2, D113) → `0618f37` viewport KeyMap guard (D2) → `6aa865d` paste routed to the focused field (D3) → `e65ab2f` colour profile from Bubble Tea, `termenv` removed (F) → `103e80b` fix: paste into every focused field of the forge explorer → `1958602` chore: import groups → `e44dcb0` redraw measure repaired (D114).
161	
162	The order differs from the plan (`A1 A2 B C D1 D2 D3 E F G1`): E came before C, and the Rule 135 fix and the explorer paste fix came after the category they belong to, noted in their bodies.
163	
164	Architecture: option C, see D111.
165	
166	**D111 — DEVDESK-201: views are `Render() string` plus `View() tea.View`; the router alone sets the terminal state. Option C, chosen by the user. Decided.** **Plane:** DEVDESK-201, dated 2026-11-10
167	
168	Three options were on the table (impact report §3, `.claude/plans/charm-v2-impact.md`):
169	- **A.** Every view returns `tea.View` and the router reads `.Content`. Rejected: the test suite's `.View()` calls become `.View().Content` (about 400 sites), and every view carries terminal fields.
170	- **B.** One `tea.Model` (`*App`) for the whole application, with the views as plain renderers (backlog §3.19). Rejected: it changes the `handle*` functions, which return `(tea.Model, tea.Cmd)` and are governed by Rule 201 (extract any `case` over five lines). The impact report counts about 480 such signatures.
171	- **C.** Each top-level view keeps its rendering in `Render() string` and exposes `View() tea.View { return tea.NewView(m.Render()) }`. The router holds `map[command.ViewType]Screen`, where `Screen` is `tea.Model` plus `Render() string`, and sets `AltScreen` in `App.View` only. Components (`datatable`, forms, `FilterBar`) keep `View() string`.

D39, before them, was the registry browser addressing a group's
members one way to browse them and another way to pull them; it is closed by
[§3.18](#318-a-registry-member-is-an-address-not-a-url--repo_prefix), which is
what it existed for. D40, found the same day and on the same screen, was the
thing §3.18 blocked on and had already been closed on its own.

D1 through D61 are all fixed or, in D35's case, deliberately
downgraded to a stale reading with a way to refresh it. §1.1 records what each was and why the
chosen fix was the right one — including the three that were answered by
*removing* something rather than making it work: D8's write-only CRUD flags,
D21's unreachable clamp and D36's never-filled cache.

The five that stayed open longest — D4, D8, D9, D10 and D11 — were parked not
because they were hard but because each altered something the user already saw,
so they needed a deliberate call rather than a drive-by fix. All five were then
decided together and fixed in one pass; see [§1.2](#12-the-five-parked-defects).

### 1.1 Fixed

**D117 — DEVDESK-201: what is not covered by a test, and what only a person can check. Open.** **Plane:** DEVDESK-201, dated 2026-11-10

Not covered by a test, to decide before the story closes: (a) the guard that a key is read through `String()` only (DEVDESK-200) does not cover `.Code`, `.Text` and `.Mod`; either a guard is added or the gap is accepted; (b) 15 `lipgloss.Place` call sites have no dedicated test (the Rule 115 test covers the confirm modal only); (c) `tea.PasteStartMsg` and `tea.PasteEndMsg` are ignored without a test.

Manual checks, run by the user and not by the agents (no TTY in the sandbox), on Windows Terminal (`dk.exe`) and WSL in Windows Terminal: the four `tea.ExecProcess` calls (container shell `T`, OCI launch `-it`, viewer pager `V`, workspace terminal `T`: alt screen restored, colours intact, no stray output); `dk setup` (alt screen, fields, space on its confirm, paste); space in every checkbox form; paste in the palette, a filter bar and a form, multi-line paste in a single-line field; one uppercase action (`S` in `ws`) and `ctrl+r`; colours under WSL with and without `NO_COLOR=1`; a VS16 emoji and a Nerd Font icon column with no shift (mode 2027); the textinput cursor background (Rule 115).

**D116 — DEVDESK-201: the prudent defaults taken without asking (H2, H3, H4, H6). Decided, to confirm.** **Plane:** DEVDESK-201, dated 2026-11-10

- **H2.** The `internal/testutil/colorprofile` helper is a no-op from A2 (`lipgloss.SetColorProfile` does not exist in v2), so the theme, overlay, shortcut, datatable and components tests compile. It is removed in F (`e65ab2f`), with `termenv`. The plan kept it as a no-op for its 50 callers; the branch deletes it.
- **H3.** `LoadTheme` refuses the whole theme when a non-empty value is not `#rgb` or `#rrggbb`, and the error names the key and the value. An empty optional key keeps the fallback. Callers are unchanged: `main.go` logs and keeps the default theme, `App.applyThemeNow` logs and keeps the current one. No footer message: a follow-up if wanted.
- **H4.** `main.go` forces `tea.WithColorProfile(colorprofile.TrueColor)` when `WT_SESSION` is set and `NO_COLOR` is not. A forced profile bypasses the `NO_COLOR` check of `colorprofile.Detect`, so the condition is explicit. The `COLORTERM` workaround is deleted.
- **H6.** `App.setView(name, m tea.Model)` is the only place that asserts `Screen`. A view that does not implement `Render` panics with the view's name; Bubble Tea recovers and restores the terminal.

**D115 — DEVDESK-201: three claims of the plan that the branch does not support as written.** **Plane:** DEVDESK-201, dated 2026-11-10

1. *The red proof for the `(4)` criterion.* The plan wanted the test that pins the width of a flag or ZWJ sequence to be red on the v2 code before the fix. It was in fact red on `go-runewidth` v0.0.16, the pre-migration version: `x/ansi` v0.11.9 already brings `go-runewidth` v0.0.30 with the v2 stack, so the red state was never shown on v2. Re-check on the migrated code before merge.
2. *Width divergence between libraries.* `datatable` measures with `go-runewidth` and the terminal-facing `x/ansi` measures differently for VS16 emoji (`a❤️x`: 3 against 4; `✔️`: 1 against 2). The divergence is pinned by `REDACTED`, so a library fix shows up as a test change.
3. *"Identical rendering" of the `ntcharts` sparkline.* Identical glyphs, not identical bytes: the background SGR goes from `48` to `49` and the reset is `\x1b[m`. The plan's "rendu identique" means the cells, not the escape sequences.

Also lost: the background of the textinput virtual cursor (Rule 115). bubbles v2 `CursorStyle` has no background; the gap is accepted until the manual check of D117.

**D114 — DEVDESK-201: the redraw cost of Bubble Tea v2 against v1 (`TestMeasureRedrawCost`). Measured; the threshold is +25 %; the verdict is within it.** **Plane:** DEVDESK-201 (G2), analysis DEVDESK-201 (perf)

Threshold chosen by the user from the three options of the plan (report only; +25 % on bytes/s of `blink-20` or `spinner-20` and no more redraws than the tick cadence). The v2 renderer also writes terminal queries and synchronized-output brackets that v1 does not, so "no worse than v1" would fail on bytes that cost nothing on screen.

Bytes/s, medians of 3 runs, interleaved on the same machine (the D110 host). v1 TrueColor is forced (D110 correction); v1 Ascii is the unforced base. Redraws: 2/s for blink, 10/s for spinner, identical in all three.

| Case | v1 Ascii B/s | v1 TrueColor B/s | v2 B/s | v2 vs v1 Ascii | v2 vs v1 TrueColor |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| blink-0 | 0 | 0 | 0 | = | = |
| blink-1 | 376 | not measured | 84 | −78 % | not measured |
| blink-20 | 5809 | 11890 | 1726 | −70 % | −85 % |
| spinner-1 | 1880 | not measured | 420 | −78 % | not measured |
| spinner-20 | 29046 | 59450 | 8629 | −70 % | −85 % |

Bytes per redraw (20-row cases): 2905 Ascii, 5945 TrueColor, 863 v2. v2 repaints changed cells only; v1 rewrote lines.

- **Verdict:** within the threshold against either base. Bytes are −70 % or better (Ascii), −85 % (TrueColor), and redraws equal the tick cadence. Nothing rises.
- **`View()` cost (D114 perf analysis, DEVDESK-201).** Isolated benchmark, `GOMAXPROCS=1`, 7 interleaved runs: v1 Ascii 288 µs, v1 TrueColor 683 µs, v2 868 µs. Real surcharge against v1 TrueColor: **+27 %**. The "×2.5–3" of the first measure is mostly an artefact: 12 to 60 cold calls, no warm-up. In-program: about 1.5 ms (v1 TrueColor) against about 2.0 ms cold (v2).
- **Cause.** `x/ansi` `stringWidth` (since v0.11.7) walks every character through grapheme segmentation, ASCII included: 240 ns to 1310 ns on a 116-column ASCII line; its share of `View()` goes from 30 % to 67 %. The v1 colour conversion (36 % of v1, via go-colorful and `Sscanf`) disappears. The theme code converts nothing per frame. The cost sits in a library: bubbletea v2.1.1 requires `x/ansi` v0.11.9, so it is not avoidable short of an upstream change.
- **Impact.** About 0.87 ms warm (about 2 ms cold) per 120×40 frame: 5–13 % of the 16 ms budget, about 2 % of one core at 10 Hz, +0.5 % CPU against v1 TrueColor. **Non-blocking.**
- **Not applied (options).** Upstream ASCII shortcut in `charmbracelet/x` `ansi/width.go` (estimated −45 to −55 % on `View`), to report upstream only if the user decides so. `view.go:117-121` redundant `Style.Width` (−6 %, but it changes the padding background: Rule 115, visual check). `lipgloss.Place` in `view.go:34-35` (at most 7 %). Compare the `redraw_measure_test.go` harness under v1 TrueColor for a fair base.
- **Harness defect fixed.** Without a TTY, v2 sends its own `WindowSizeMsg` built from a 0×0 size, which shrinks the router to a 489-byte view. The fix is `tea.WithWindowSize(...)` and `tea.WithColorProfile(colorprofile.TrueColor)` in `measureRedraws` (`e44dcb0`).
- **Limits.** In-process, no TTY: this counts what the renderer writes, not what a terminal shows. The v2 mode queries and synchronized output are not exercised; the real-SSH check stays with A-06. The `View()` study uses a dummy 120×40 view on one machine; real views are not profiled.

**D113 — DEVDESK-201: Rule 135 corrected in the PR. Enter does nothing on a checkbox; Space no longer answers Yes or No on a confirmation. Decided (prudent choice on a destructive modal, to confirm).** **Plane:** DEVDESK-201 (`ad0900d`), dated 2026-11-10

Rule 135 gives `Space` alone the tick on a checkbox and `Enter` alone the validation of action buttons. The v2 port exposed two places where the rule was not applied:
- Enter toggled a checkbox. It is now ignored on a checkbox cell.
- Space answered the focused Yes or No button of `OptionConfirmModal`, `ConfirmModal`, `ChoiceModal` and the setup wizard's `confirm`. It no longer does.

Choice on a destructive modal: Enter on a focused cell is ignored rather than advancing to the next step, so a stray Enter cannot confirm a delete. The alternative (Enter advances, as on any other button) is open to the user; it changes one line per modal.

Rule 135 text to be corrected by the tech-writer (G1): the Space line becomes `keymap.Space` is `"space"`, the key is matched through the constant.

**D112 — DEVDESK-201: the Charm v2 migration lands as one pull request, in categories; the commits are review units. Decided.** **Plane:** DEVDESK-201, dated 2026-11-10

One PR, squash-merged, with the commits listed in its body. The commits split the migration by category, not by file, and they are not bisect points: `internal/app` imports every view, so no commit between the imports change and the theme change builds the whole module. Real order on `feat/DEVDESK-201-charm-v2`, after `origin/main` `f8c3063`:

`7091e78` imports and `go.mod` (A1) → `a74a262` theme `color.Color` and hex validation (A2) → `0692c35` keys, `KeyPressMsg`, `keymap.Space = "space"` (B) → `ba1d938` Bubbles and Lip Gloss APIs (D1) → `495409b` ntcharts v2 and module tidy (E) → `89f32a3` `Render` and `View() tea.View`, router owns `AltScreen` (C) → `dab9d28` fix: nil `confirmModal` guard removed from the setup wizard render → `ad0900d` Rule 135 (B2, D113) → `0618f37` viewport KeyMap guard (D2) → `6aa865d` paste routed to the focused field (D3) → `e65ab2f` colour profile from Bubble Tea, `termenv` removed (F) → `103e80b` fix: paste into every focused field of the forge explorer → `1958602` chore: import groups → `e44dcb0` redraw measure repaired (D114).

The order differs from the plan (`A1 A2 B C D1 D2 D3 E F G1`): E came before C, and the Rule 135 fix and the explorer paste fix came after the category they belong to, noted in their bodies.

Architecture: option C, see D111.

**D111 — DEVDESK-201: views are `Render() string` plus `View() tea.View`; the router alone sets the terminal state. Option C, chosen by the user. Decided.** **Plane:** DEVDESK-201, dated 2026-11-10

Three options were on the table (impact report §3, `.claude/plans/charm-v2-impact.md`):
- **A.** Every view returns `tea.View` and the router reads `.Content`. Rejected: the test suite's `.View()` calls become `.View().Content` (about 400 sites), and every view carries terminal fields.
- **B.** One `tea.Model` (`*App`) for the whole application, with the views as plain renderers (backlog §3.19). Rejected: it changes the `handle*` functions, which return `(tea.Model, tea.Cmd)` and are governed by Rule 201 (extract any `case` over five lines). The impact report counts about 480 such signatures.
- **C.** Each top-level view keeps its rendering in `Render() string` and exposes `View() tea.View { return tea.NewView(m.Render()) }`. The router holds `map[command.ViewType]Screen`, where `Screen` is `tea.Model` plus `Render() string`, and sets `AltScreen` in `App.View` only. Components (`datatable`, forms, `FilterBar`) keep `View() string`.

Why C: fewest changes; the compiler guides the test sites; no `handle*` signature moves (the plan's survey counts 271 `handle*` and 429 returns of `(tea.Model, tea.Cmd)`, a recount is due); the terminal state is declared in one place. The two `tea.WithAltScreen()` calls (`main.go`, `setup/wizard.go`) are gone.

Consequence: a view that does not implement `Render` panics in `setView` (D116, H6), and a table test covers every `ViewType`. No ADR: the repository has no `docs/decisions/` or `docs/adr/` folder, and the project keeps its lasting decisions here (D entries).

**D110 — Redraw cost reference on Bubble Tea v1.3.10, taken before the v2 move. Measured.** **Plane:** DEVDESK-200 (criterion 7)

> **Correction (2026-11-10, DEVDESK-201, D114 analysis).** (a) The v1 base of this table ran with the Ascii profile, not forced TrueColor: `go test` has no TTY, and Lip Gloss v1 converted no colour. Forced TrueColor on v1 gives 5945 bytes per redraw (20 rows) and about 1.5 ms of `View()` in-program; v2 gives 863 bytes: −85 % against v1 TrueColor (−70 % against the Ascii base). (b) The "×2.5–3" `View()` ratio of this entry is mostly a cold-call artefact (12 to 60 calls). Isolated benchmark, `GOMAXPROCS=1`: v1 Ascii 288 µs, v1 TrueColor 683 µs, v2 868 µs: a real +27 % against TrueColor. (c) The rest is in `x/ansi` (see D114). The figures above are not rewritten.

`TestMeasureRedrawCost` now also reports redraws per second, bytes per redraw and the mean `View()` time (a redraw is one `Write`: the v1 renderer flushes once per frame; the program calls `View()` after every `Update`). Medians of 3 runs, 6 s window after a 2 s warm-up, terminal 120x40, 36 rows per view (`blink-N` / `spinner-N`: N animated rows; blink at 1 Hz means 2 phase changes per second).

| Case | bytes/s | redraws/s | bytes/redraw | mean `View()` |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| blink-0 | 0 | 0 | 0 | n/a (no call) |
| blink-1 | 376 | 2.0 | 188 | 706 µs |
| blink-20 | 5810 | 2.0 | 2905 | 832 µs |
| spinner-1 | 1880 | 10.0 | 188 | 764 µs |
| spinner-20 | 29046 | 10.0 | 2905 | 757 µs |

arbre bougeait donc quand on renommait un dossier ailleurs. Le parcours ne
compte plus que les fichiers réguliers.

Ce qui compte autant que le défaut : `TestSizeDoesNotFollowSymlinks` existait, et
il **se saute sous Windows**, où créer un lien demande un privilège que le compte
de test n'a pas. Il n'a donc jamais tourné sur la machine de développement, et
c'est CI — Linux — qui l'a exécuté pour la première fois. Un test qui se saute
sur la seule machine où on le lance ne dit rien du tout, et rien ne le signale.

Deferred: workspace hygiene (`3 dirty, 2 behind`, §3.17). Right data, but the
walk cost grows with the repository count. Rejected: listening ports — `ss`
needs a privileged container.

#### Bubble Tea v2 is deliberately not bundled

v2 is GA (bubbletea v2.0.8, lipgloss v2.0.6, bubbles v2.1.1); v1 is not
deprecated; and **nothing here needs v2** — ntcharts v0.5.1 delivers braille and
multi-series stream charts on v1, verified by running it.

The reason for separating them, above all others: in v2 `msg.String()` returns
`"space"` instead of `" "`, and there are **10 `case " ":` across 10 files**. The
compiler says nothing — `case " ":` stays valid Go and simply stops matching.
Rule 135 makes `Space` the only key allowed to tick a checkbox, so a careless
migration silently breaks every checkbox in the application. That has to surface
in a pull request that does nothing else.

| Migration work | Extent | Nature |
|---|---|---|
| Imports → `charm.land/*/v2` | 154 files / 301 | mechanical |
| `tea.KeyMsg` → `tea.KeyPressMsg` | 96 | compiler-found |
| `View() string` → `View() tea.View` | 11 views + router | **architecture** |
| `lipgloss.Color` as a type → `color.Color` | 46, nearly all in `colors.go` | one file |
| `WithWhitespaceBackground` → `WithWhitespaceStyle` | 13 | mechanical |
| `AdaptiveColor` / `TerminalColor` | 0 | no `compat` needed |

lipgloss v2's largest change to one file, and `datatable` rendering its own rows

architecture is that the router types views as `tea.Model` (`app.go:47`); the
better answer is the inverse — DevDesk declares its own `View` interface and
